input: What is the purpose of FADEC and what does it replace in piston-engined aircraft?

input: How do winglets reduce induced drag, and what is the aerodynamic trade-off of fitting them?
expected_output: Winglets reduce induced drag by weakening the wingtip vortex - the spanwise flow that rolls up around the tip - which cuts the downwash behind the wing and tilts the lift vector forward, recovering some of the energy otherwise lost to the vortex. The trade-off is added wetted area and therefore more parasite drag, plus extra structural weight and higher root bending moment, so the net benefit only appears at higher lift coefficients, which is why the gain shows up in cruise and climb rather than in high-speed low-altitude flight.

input: What is V1 in takeoff performance, and why is it not simply a fixed speed for a given aircraft type?
expected_output: V1 is the takeoff decision speed: the maximum speed at which the crew can initiate a reject and still stop within the remaining accelerate-stop distance, and equally the minimum speed from which the takeoff can be continued on the remaining engine after a failure. It is not fixed per type because it is recomputed for every departure from runway length and slope, aircraft weight, flap setting, air density, wind component, and runway surface condition - so the same airframe can have a materially different V1 on two different days or runways.
